target_customer: Restaurants and F&B groups in Singapore and Southeast Asia
problem: Restaurants juggle separate POS, online ordering, kitchen and delivery tools. Atlas bundles them into one operating system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription from about 79 to 89 dollars per month plus payments and logistics

founders.name: Yi Sung (Sung) Yong
previous_startups: Grain (online restaurant, raised a Series B)

competitors.name: StoreHub
competitors.what: Malaysian POS and online ordering for retail and F&B across SEA
competitors.funding_then: About $15M total as of Jan 2020 per its blog

competitors.name: Qashier
competitors.what: Smart POS that added online ordering and delivery in Covid
competitors.funding_then: US$10M Series A, date not given in the source

technical_complexity.rationale: POS, kitchen display, aggregator syncing and logistics integrations are standard but wide in scope for a small team, with hardware and payments partners needed.

defensibility.rationale: POS replacement is sticky once installed and the team brings operator credibility from Grain, but competitors had similar bundles and funding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying evidence found. Regional rivals kept raising; FeedMe raised $5M in Nov 2025 (later, not as of founding).

market_need_then: Covid pushed restaurants online in 2020 and 2021, and the founders say they ran Grain, a cloud kitchen, and productised its tech stack. A 2019 TechCrunch-sourced piece described the Grain Atlas stack, per a search summary.

branding.domain_note: Uses atlas.kitchen, a descriptive .kitchen TLD rather than atlas.com.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and playful, calls itself a love letter to restaurants, uses Singapore references and wordplay (company site).

branding.community_and_virality: Adyen announced a partnership in July 2025 per a search summary; no community or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A common word with unrelated businesses such as a Singapore bar named ATLAS, partly offset by a distinctive .kitchen domain and warm voice. No press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Atlas is still operating in Singapore with named customers such as Raffles Hotel, Haidilao and SaladStop, and its founders bring operating experience from Grain. No credible funding figures or exit exist in the sources, so growth is visible only through customers and headcount, which differs between sources. It competes in a crowded regional POS market against better funded rivals.
notes: Aggregator funding totals conflict (CB Insights $130K, Village.ai $3.1M, a job board $6.0M seed), so none are recorded as rounds. Team size 12 on YC versus 23 on Built In, undated. Founder education not found. Competitors StoreHub dated Jan 2020 (before batch).
